51.solution: A conjugate acid-base pair differs by exactly one proton: the acid has one more \(\mathrm{H^+}\) than its conjugate base. In \(\mathrm{HSO_3^{-} + H_3O^{+} \rightleftharpoons H_2SO_3 + H_2O}\), \(\mathrm{HSO_3^{-}}\) accepts a proton to become \(\mathrm{H_2SO_3}\); so \(\mathrm{H_2SO_3}\) (acid) and \(\mathrm{HSO_3^{-}}\) (base) form a conjugate pair.

52.solution: Reactivity in aromatic nucleophilic substitution increases with the number of strong electron-withdrawing groups at the ortho/para positions, which stabilise the carbanion (Meisenheimer) intermediate. 2,4,6-Trinitrochlorobenzene has three \(-\mathrm{NO_2}\) groups at o/p positions, so it is the most reactive.

53.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
53.solution: A Grignard reagent adds to \(\mathrm{CO_2}\) and after acidic work-up gives a carboxylic acid with one more carbon than the alkyl group. \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CHMgBr}\) (isopropyl) gives \(\mathrm{(CH_3)_2CH{-}COOH}\), i.e. 2-methylpropanoic acid (isobutyric acid).

54.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
54.solution: The electrode with the higher (less negative) reduction potential is the cathode. \(E^{\circ}_{cell} = E^{\circ}_{cathode} - E^{\circ}_{anode} = E^{\circ}_{Sn} - E^{\circ}_{Fe} = (-0.14) - (-0.44) = +0.30\ \mathrm{V}\).

55.subtopic: Molecular Orbital Theory and Bond Order
55.solution: Number of electrons in antibonding MOs: \(\mathrm{Li_2}\) has 2 \((\sigma^{*}1s)^2\); \(\mathrm{N_2}\) has 4; \(\mathrm{O_2}\) has 6 \((\sigma^{*}1s)^2(\sigma^{*}2s)^2(\pi^{*}2p)^2\); \(\mathrm{F_2}\) has 8 \((\sigma^{*}1s)^2(\sigma^{*}2s)^2(\pi^{*}2p)^4\). \(\mathrm{F_2}\) has the maximum.

56.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
56.solution: Pressure-volume work \(W = -\Delta n_g RT\); it is negative when \(\Delta n_g > 0\) (gas expands). For \(\mathrm{2H_2O_2(l) \to 2H_2O(l) + O_2(g)}\), \(\Delta n_g = 1 - 0 = +1\), so \(W = -RT < 0\). The other reactions have \(\Delta n_g \le 0\) (gas moles decrease), giving zero or positive work.

57.solution: Packing efficiency of an fcc cell is \(74\%\) for the 4 atoms it contains. Volume occupied by one atom \(= \dfrac{0.74}{4} \times (1.6\times 10^{-23}) = 0.185 \times 1.6\times 10^{-23} = 2.96\times 10^{-24}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).
57.stemOverride: Calculate the volume occupied by a particle in fcc unit cell if volume of unit cell is \(1.6 \times 10^{-23}\ \mathrm{cm^3}\).
57.note: Stem cell volume lost its leading digit in extraction ('.6' \(\to\) intended \(1.6\times10^{-23}\)); restored so the answer \(2.96\times10^{-24}\) (= 0.74/4 \(\times\) cell volume) is reproducible. Key B correct.

58.solution: Alanine has the structure \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH(NH_2){-}COOH}\); its side chain is \(-\mathrm{CH_3}\). Leucine has an isobutyl side chain, serine \(-\mathrm{CH_2OH}\), and valine an isopropyl side chain.

59.subtopic: Green Chemistry, Principles, Atom Economy and Green Solvents
59.solution: Curcumin, the active constituent of turmeric, is well known for its antiseptic property.

60.solution: Atomic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group. Mg (period 3, group 2) is smallest; Na > Mg; K is below Na; Rb is below K. Increasing order: \(\mathrm{Mg < Na < K < Rb}\).
60.stemOverride: Which is the correct increasing order of atomic radii of Na, K, Mg, Rb?
60.note: Stem element 'a' is a dropped 'Na'; restored. Key B correct.

61.subtopic: Inner Transition Elements, Lanthanoids and Actinoids
61.solution: First ionisation enthalpies (kJ/mol): La \(\approx 538\), Ce \(\approx 534\), Gd \(\approx 593\), Yb \(\approx 603\). The relatively high value of Yb arises from its filled \(4f^{14}\) configuration. Hence Yb has the highest \(IE_1\).

62.subtopic: Carboxylic Acids, Properties, Reactions and Derivatives
62.solution: Carboxylic acids react with \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\) to give the acid chloride along with \(\mathrm{POCl_3}\) and \(\mathrm{HCl}\): \(\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH + PCl_5 \to C_6H_5COCl + POCl_3 + HCl}\). The reagent is \(\mathrm{PCl_5}\).

63.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
63.solution: For the oxidation \(\mathrm{Al \to Al^{3+}(0.1\,M) + 3e^{-}}\), the standard oxidation potential is \(+1.66\ \mathrm{V}\). By Nernst, \(E = E^{\circ}_{ox} - \dfrac{0.0592}{3}\log[\mathrm{Al^{3+}}] = 1.66 - \dfrac{0.0592}{3}\log(0.1) = 1.66 - 0.0197(-1) = 1.66 + 0.0197 = +1.679\ \mathrm{V}\).

64.solution: For a 1:4 mass ratio of \(\mathrm{O_2:CH_4}\), molecules \(\propto\) moles \(= \dfrac{\text{mass}}{M}\). \(\dfrac{N_{O_2}}{N_{CH_4}} = \dfrac{1/32}{4/16} = \dfrac{1/32}{1/4} = \dfrac{1}{8}\). Ratio \(= 1:8\).

65.solution: Relative lowering of vapour pressure \(= \dfrac{W_2 M_1}{M_2 W_1} = \dfrac{3 \times 18}{60 \times 50} = \dfrac{54}{3000} = 0.018\).

66.subtopic: Crystal Defects, Magnetic Properties and Semiconductors
66.solution: Brass is an alloy of Cu and Zn in which Zn atoms (similar size to Cu) replace Cu atoms at lattice sites. This is a substitutional impurity defect.

67.subtopic: Diazonium Salts and Aromatic Amine Reactions
67.solution: Azo coupling is the reaction of a diazonium salt with an electron-rich arene (phenol or aromatic amine) to give an azo compound. Benzenediazonium chloride couples with phenol to give p-hydroxyazobenzene (\(\mathrm{C_6H_5{-}N{=}N{-}C_6H_4OH}\)).

68.subtopic: Nomenclature, Structural Isomers and Physical Properties
68.solution: Undecane \((\mathrm{C_{11}H_{24}})\) and decane \((\mathrm{C_{10}H_{22}})\) are successive members of the alkane homologous series, differing by one \(-\mathrm{CH_2}-\) unit, i.e. \(14\ \mathrm{g\,mol^{-1}}\).

69.subtopic: Polyhalogen Compounds — Freon, DDT, War Gases
69.solution: BHC (benzene hexachloride, gammexane/lindane) is an effective insecticide used in place of DDT.

70.solution: Atomic ratio \(\mathrm{Xe:F} = 0.4:2.4 = 1:6\), so the compound is \(\mathrm{XeF_6}\). With F as \(-1\): \(x + 6(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6\).

71.subtopic: Ionic Equilibrium, Ka, Kb and Degree of Dissociation

72.subtopic: Nomenclature, Hybridization and Stability of Alkenes
72.solution: Cis-trans isomerism requires each doubly-bonded carbon to bear two different groups. In but-1-ene \(\mathrm{CH_3CH_2{-}CH{=}CH_2}\) the terminal carbon has two identical H atoms, so no geometric isomerism. But-2-ene, pent-2-ene and 3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene all show cis-trans isomerism.

73.subtopic: Preparation Methods of Aldehydes and Ketones
73.solution: Reduction of a nitrile with DIBAL-H \((\mathrm{AlH(i\text{-}Bu)_2})\) followed by hydrolysis gives an aldehyde with the same carbon skeleton. Pent-3-enal \(\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CHCH_2CHO}\) therefore comes from pent-3-enenitrile \(\mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CHCH_2C{\equiv}N}\).

74.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
74.solution: Benzene-1,4-diol (hydroquinone) is commonly called quinol. (Catechol = 1,2-diol; resorcinol = 1,3-diol; pyrogallol = 1,2,3-triol.)

75.solution: In a halous acid the halogen is in the \(+3\) oxidation state. For chlorine this is chlorous acid, \(\mathrm{HClO_2}\).

76.subtopic: Thermochemistry, Hess's Law and Bond Enthalpy

77.solution: Number of atoms in mass \(x = \dfrac{x \cdot n}{\rho a^3}\). For fcc, \(n = 4\). Atoms in 1 g \(= \dfrac{1 \times 4}{6.8\times 10^{-22}} = 5.882\times 10^{21}\).

78.subtopic: Glycosidic Linkages in Di- and Polysaccharides
78.solution: In sucrose the glycosidic bond forms between C-1 of \(\alpha\)-D-glucose (anomeric/aldehyde carbon) and C-2 of \(\beta\)-D-fructose (anomeric/keto carbon). So the carbons are C-1 and C-2 respectively.

79.subtopic: Oxidation State, Coordination Number and IUPAC Nomenclature
79.solution: An octahedral complex has six ligand donor atoms around the central metal ion, so the coordination number is 6 (\(d^2sp^3\) or \(sp^3d^2\) hybridisation).

80.subtopic: Rate of Reaction, Stoichiometry and Average Rate
80.solution: For \(\mathrm{2NO + 2H_2 \to N_2 + 2H_2O}\), rate \(= -\tfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{NO}]}{dt} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt} = \dfrac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = \tfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2O}]}{dt}\). Hence \(\dfrac{d[\mathrm{N_2}]}{dt} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d[\mathrm{H_2}]}{dt}\), which is option B.

82.solution: In a haloalkyne the halogen is bonded to an sp-hybridised carbon of the triple bond (e.g. \(\mathrm{X{-}C{\equiv}C{-}R}\)). Hence the halogen is on an sp carbon.

83.subtopic: IUPAC and Common Nomenclature of Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
83.solution: Catechol is the 1,2-dihydroxybenzene, so its IUPAC name is benzene-1,2-diol.

84.solution: Fluorine, being the most electronegative element, can show only the \(-1\) oxidation state in compounds with oxygen and forms a single oxoacid, hypofluorous acid \(\mathrm{HOF}\). Chlorine shows multiple positive oxidation states (\(+1,+3,+5,+7\)) and forms four oxoacids: \(\mathrm{HOCl, HClO_2, HClO_3, HClO_4}\) — the maximum number. Hence Cl forms the maximum number of oxoacids.
84.note: AK key A (F) is wrong and contradicts standard chemistry. Fluorine forms only ONE oxoacid (HOF), the fewest of all halogens, because it cannot take positive oxidation states. Chlorine forms FOUR oxoacids (HOCl, HClO2, HClO3, HClO4) — the maximum. Correct answer is B (Cl).

85.subtopic: First Law of Thermodynamics, Internal Energy and Work
85.solution: First law: \(\Delta U = Q + W\). Work done on the system \(W = +20\ \mathrm{kJ}\); heat released by the system \(Q = -10\ \mathrm{kJ}\). \(\Delta U = -10 + 20 = +10\ \mathrm{kJ}\).

86.solution: \(\Delta T_b = i K_b m\); with \(K_b\) constant, compare \(i\,m\): KCl \(2\times0.2 = 0.4\); NaCl \(2\times0.1 = 0.2\); \(\mathrm{AlCl_3}\) \(4\times1 = 4\); \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\) \(3\times0.05 = 0.15\). The minimum \(i\,m\) (0.15, for \(\mathrm{MgCl_2}\)) gives the minimum boiling-point elevation.

87.solution: Neoprene is polychloroprene, the addition polymer of chloroprene, 2-chloro-1,3-butadiene.

88.solution: Carbonyl (CO) is a neutral ligand. Sulphato \((\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}})\), oxalato \((\mathrm{C_2O_4^{2-}})\) and bromo \((\mathrm{Br^{-}})\) are anionic ligands.

89.solution: The Fischer-Tropsch synthesis of gasoline from water gas uses a cobalt-thoria (Co-Th, with kieselguhr) catalyst.

90.subtopic: Rate Law, Order, Molecularity and Rate Expression
90.solution: Overall order is the sum of the exponents in the rate law: \(1.5 + 2.5 = 4\).

91.subtopic: Colloids, Classification, Coagulation and Hardy-Schulze Rule
91.solution: By the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion increases with the magnitude of its charge opposite to the sol. For a positive sol, the most negatively charged anion is most effective. \([\mathrm{Fe(CN)_6}]^{4-}\) (charge \(-4\)) has the highest coagulating power.

92.solution: An allylic halide has X on the \(sp^3\) carbon directly adjacent to a \(\mathrm{C{=}C}\). In A, B and C the \(\mathrm{CH_2{-}X}\) is next to the double bond (allylic). In D, \(\mathrm{CH_3{-}CH{=}CH{-}CH_2{-}CH_2{-}X}\), the C bearing X is two carbons from the double bond (homoallylic), so it is NOT an allylic halide.

93.subtopic: Diazonium Salts and Aromatic Amine Reactions
93.solution: Aniline with \(\mathrm{NaNO_2/HCl}\) at 273 K gives benzenediazonium chloride (A). On warming with water it hydrolyses, releasing \(\mathrm{N_2}\) and giving phenol (B): \(\mathrm{C_6H_5N_2^{+}Cl^{-} + H_2O \xrightarrow{\Delta} C_6H_5OH + N_2 + HCl}\).

94.subtopic: Galvanic Cells, EMF, Nernst Equation and Thermodynamics
94.solution: The strongest oxidising agent has the highest standard reduction potential and the greatest tendency to be reduced. \(\mathrm{F_2}\) has the highest \(E^{\circ}\) among the species, so it is the strongest oxidising agent.

95.subtopic: Subatomic Particles, Isotopes, Isobars and Isoelectronic Species
95.solution: Isoelectronic species have the same number of electrons. Ne has 10 electrons and \(\mathrm{O^{2-}}\) (8 + 2) also has 10, so they are isoelectronic.

96.solution: \(m = \dfrac{\Delta T_b}{K_b} = \dfrac{0.6}{2} = 0.3\ \mathrm{mol\,kg^{-1}}\). Since \(m = \dfrac{\text{moles solute}}{\text{mass solvent (kg)}}\), mass of solvent \(= \dfrac{0.01}{0.3} = 0.033\ \mathrm{kg}\).

97.solution: The \(-\mathrm{CO{-}NH}-\) (amide) linkage is present in urea-formaldehyde resin \((\mathrm{[-NH{-}CO{-}NH{-}CH_2-]_n})\). Glyptal (polyester), thermocol (polystyrene) and Buna-N (copolymer of butadiene and acrylonitrile) lack the amide linkage.

98.subtopic: Chemical Reactions and Basicity of Amines
98.solution: Highest \(pK_b\) means the weakest base. In aniline \((\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2})\) the nitrogen lone pair is delocalised into the benzene ring, reducing its availability, so aniline is the weakest base and has the highest \(pK_b\).

99.subtopic: First-Order Kinetics, Rate Constant and Half-Life
99.solution: For first order, \(k = \dfrac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}\), so \(k \propto \dfrac{1}{t_{1/2}}\). With \((t_{1/2})_A = 75\ \mathrm{min}\) and \((t_{1/2})_B = 2.5\ \mathrm{h} = 150\ \mathrm{min}\), the ratio of rate constants \(= \dfrac{(t_{1/2})_B}{(t_{1/2})_A} = \dfrac{150}{75} = 2.0\). Among the options only 2.0 is consistent with the intended computation.
99.note: Stem labels the asked ratio as r_B/r_A but the AK solution computes 150/75 = 2 (which is k_A/k_B). The literal k_B/k_A = 0.5 is not among the options; the intended value, 2.0 (option A), is the only viable choice, so the answer is A. Printed-paper labelling inconsistency, not a key error.

100.solution: Moles in 1 mL \((=10^{-3}\ \mathrm{L})\) of vapour at STP \(= \dfrac{10^{-3}}{22.4} = 4.46\times 10^{-5}\ \mathrm{mol}\). Molecules \(= 4.46\times 10^{-5} \times 6.022\times 10^{23} = 2.69\times 10^{19}\).
